question.problem: Anna makes two cakes. The first cake weighs $1,200\,\text{g},$ while the second cake weighs $140%$ of the weight of the first. What is the weight of the second cake?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the weight of the first cake, which is $1,200\,\text{g}.$ The percentage is $140%,$ and the part is the weight of the second cake.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
140%=140÷100=1.4
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =140%\times 1,200 \\  & =1.4\times 1,200 \\  & =1,680\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $140%$ of $1,200$ is $1,680.$ So, the weight of the second cake is $1,680\,\text{g}.$

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
140%=\frac{140}{100}=\frac{140÷20}{100÷20}=\frac{7}{5}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =140%\times 1,200 \\  & =\frac{7}{5}\times 1,200 \\  & =7\times \frac{1,200}{5} \\  & =7\times 240 \\  & =1,680\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $140%$ of $1,200$ is $1,680.$ So, the weight of the second cake is $1,680\,\text{g}.$
